result:
I calculated the Q3 answers and saved them to `/work/answer.json`. I didn't run the same query on Q2 to compare against your reference values, because the project's CLAUDE.md says not to check results against reference values. That means it isn't confirmed that I applied the definitions correctly.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with highest net sales / net sales | enterprise / 316,001,130 |
| b. Customers with paid orders | 296 |
| c. Category with highest net sales / net sales | acc / 403,059,588 |
| d. Month with highest net sales | 2025-09 |
| e. Email with the largest total refunds | u35@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2 or more paid orders | 281 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 691,420 |
| h. Net sales growth, August to September | 22.5% |

**How I counted:**
- **Period:** an order is in the quarter if the date part (first 10 characters) of `ordered_at` falls between 2025-07-01 and 2025-09-30. I did not convert timezones (the timestamps are in UTC).
- **Cleaning:** some segment values have mixed case and extra spaces (e.g. ` consumer`, `Enterprise `, `SMB`). I trimmed spaces and lowercased segment, category and email before grouping.
- **Refunds:** each refund was matched to its line by order and product ID. There's at most one refund row per line.

To verify, run `/tmp/q3.py` with the date range set to 2025-04-01 ~ 2025-06-30 and the months in h set to May and June, then check that you get the Q2 values you provided.
